title: Food poisoning at a charity auction
setting: Community centre auction. Patient believes out-of-date dairy product in homemade cake caused severe food poisoning. Patient gagging, about to vomit, severe stomach pain.
verdictExplanation: High BGL, tachycardia, tachypnoea, and vomiting in a diabetic patient indicate diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) mimicking food poisoning. Sick: requires immediate hospital transfer.

history.history: Eaten a homemade cake with out-of-date dairy products 30 minutes ago

followUp.question: What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?
followUp.explanation: The patient has a history of Type 1 Diabetes and a very high blood glucose level (17.1 mmol/L). Along with abdominal pain, vomiting, and rapid breathing, this points to Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), which often mimics food poisoning. It requires immediate medical attention.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Reassure, provide sick bag. Give sips of water. Monitor closely.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ensure BGL is monitored (risk of ketoacidosis in diabetic patients). Hydrate within scope, check vitals, and prepare for onward care if severe.
